findings.fact: Issuer-hosted corrected transcript for the Aug 26 Q2 FY2027 call states the Q3 FY2027 earnings call is scheduled for Nov 17, 2026. Nov17 is BEFORE the Dec31 contract date; it is after only the Oct31 sibling date. The issuer events page fetched Oct 19 shows no listed upcoming event details in its static body (it says select a highlighted date), so the transcript is the direct captured basis for Nov 17.

The same Q2 transcript says Q3 revenue outlook is $108B ±2%, expects sequential growth primarily from ACIE and data center, and Vera Rubin at about 20% of Q3 data-center revenue. It also says FY2028 revenue preliminary expectation approximately 70% year-over-year growth. These are management outlook statements from Aug 26, not realized results.

Issuer release dated Sep 28 announces an additional $150B share-repurchase authorization, bringing remaining authorized program to $235B, with expected execution through FY2028. Authorization is capacity, not evidence of repurchases actually completed or share-count reduction by Dec 31.

The prior Oct 19 vendor snapshot in work/0364_primary_refresh_1646.json put NVIDIA first at $5.267T, Apple $4.991T, Alphabet $4.169T and Microsoft $3.962T; it has no exact exchange close timestamp or globally exhaustive private-company convention. Existing Q2 SEC share-count data is filing-dated, not a Dec 31 count.

No newer issuer-announced split or separately dated share-count change was established in this bounded pass. The captured pages do not define the contract’s credible-reporting consensus, private-company inclusion, share-class/FX treatment, or the Dec 31 source aggregation.
